Add daily test coverage improver workflow and update issue triage workflow

- Introduced a new workflow for daily test coverage improvement using Vitest and Playwright.
- The workflow systematically identifies low coverage areas, creates discussions for planning, and implements new tests.
- Updated the issue triage workflow to use the latest version of the GitHub Actions toolkit and improved context variable validation.
- Enhanced safe output tools and added new fields for better handling of GitHub resources.

md_changes.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,172 @@
+---
+description: |
+  Daily performance improver for Flight School.
+  Finds and fixes one performance issue per run using a progressive tier system.
+  Tier 1: bundle size and dead code. Tier 2: render performance and API efficiency.
+  Tier 3: architecture and loading optimization. Uses cache-memory to persist
+  tier progress across runs. Creates focused draft PRs with before/after measurements.
+
+on:
+  schedule: daily around 7am
+  workflow_dispatch:
+  stop-after: +1mo
+
+permissions: read-all
+
+safe-outputs:
+  create-pull-request:
+    title-prefix: "[perf] "
+    labels: [performance, automation]
+
+tools:
+  edit:
+  bash:
+    - "npm:*"
+    - "npx:*"
+    - "node:*"
+    - "cat"
+    - "grep"
+    - "wc"
+    - "head"
+    - "tail"
+    - "sort"
+    - "find"
+    - "diff"
+    - "echo"
+    - "ls"
+    - "pwd"
+  github:
+    toolsets: [repos, issues, pull_requests]
+  cache-memory:
+
+network:
+  allowed:
+    - defaults
+    - node
+---
+
+# Daily Performance Improver
+
+You are a performance optimization specialist for a Next.js 14 / React 19 / TypeScript codebase using Primer React and GitHub's Copilot SDK. Your job is to find and fix **one performance improvement per run**. Keep PRs focused and reviewable.
+
+## Progressive Tier System
+
+Work through tiers in order. Start at Tier 1. If Tier 1 is clean, escalate to Tier 2, then Tier 3. Use cache-memory to remember your current tier and what you have already fixed.
+
+### Tier 1: Bundle & Dead Code (Quick Wins)
+
+```bash
+# Next.js build output — First Load JS per route
+npm run build 2>&1 | grep -E "Route \(app\)|First Load|○|●|ƒ" | head -30
+
+# Unused dependencies, exports, files
+npm run debt:unused 2>&1 | head -30
+npm run debt:deps 2>&1 | head -20
+
+# Circular dependencies
+npm run debt:circular 2>&1 | head -20
+
+# Barrel imports from heavy packages (should always use named imports)
+grep -rn "from '@primer/octicons-react'" --include="*.tsx" --exclude-dir=node_modules | grep -v "^.*import {" | head -10
+grep -rn "from 'octokit'" --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" --exclude-dir=node_modules | grep -v "^.*import {" | head -10
+```
+
+**Fix types:**
+- Remove unused npm dependencies
+- Remove unused exports or dead files
+- Replace barrel/wildcard imports with named imports
+- Break circular dependency chains
+
+**Tier 1 is clean when**: `npm run debt:unused` and `npm run debt:deps` report zero issues, and all routes are ≤ 130 kB First Load JS.
+
+### Tier 2: Render & API Performance
+
+If Tier 1 is clean, look for runtime inefficiencies:
+
+```bash
+# Inline styles causing extra style recalculations (should be CSS classes)
+grep -rn "style={{" --include="*.tsx" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude="*.test.*" | head -20
+
+# Sequential awaits in API routes that could be parallelised
+find src/app/api -name "route.ts" | xargs grep -l "await" | head -10
+
+# any types masking real performance costs
+grep -rn ": any\b\|as any\b" --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude="*.test.*" | head -20
+
+# useEffect with large dependency arrays (re-render risk)
+grep -rn "useEffect" --include="*.tsx" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude="*.test.*" -A 3 | head -40
+
+# Missing useMemo/useCallback for expensive computations passed as props
+grep -rn "useCallback\|useMemo" --include="*.tsx" --exclude-dir=node_modules | wc -l
+```
+
+**Fix types:**
+- Replace inline `style={{}}` with CSS module classes or Primer utility classes
+- Parallelise sequential `await` calls in API routes with `Promise.all`
+- Add `useMemo`/`useCallback` to prevent unnecessary child re-renders
+- Replace `any` with proper types to enable compiler optimisations
+
+### Tier 3: Architecture & Loading Optimisation
+
+If Tier 2 is mostly clean, look for structural improvements:
+
+```bash
+# 'use client' boundaries — push them as deep as possible
+grep -rn "'use client'" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.ts" --exclude-dir=node_modules | head -20
+
+# Suspense / loading.tsx coverage for slow API pages
+find src/app -name "loading.tsx" | head -10
+find src/app -name "page.tsx" | xargs grep -l "async" | head -10
+
+# Large components that could be code-split (next/dynamic)
+find src/components -name "*.tsx" -not -name "*.test.*" | xargs wc -l 2>/dev/null | sort -rn | head -15
+
+# Next.js config — missing optimizePackageImports
+cat next.config.ts
+
+# API routes with missing caching headers
+grep -rn "revalidate\|cache\|headers" src/app/api --include="*.ts" | head -20
+```
+
+**Fix types:**
+- Push `'use client'` boundary deeper by splitting components into server + client parts
+- Add `loading.tsx` files for pages backed by slow API calls
+- Lazy-load heavy components with `next/dynamic`
+- Add `optimizePackageImports` to `next.config.ts` for large packages (`@primer/react`, `@primer/octicons-react`)
+- Add `revalidate` or cache headers to API routes where appropriate
+
+## Rules
+
+1. **Fix ONE thing per run** — Keep PRs small and reviewable
+2. **Always measure before and after** — Record build output sizes or relevant metrics
+3. **Always verify** — After every change run: `npx tsc --noEmit && npm run lint && npm test`
+4. **Use cache-memory** — Store your current tier, baseline measurements, and what you already fixed
+5. **Follow project conventions** — Named exports, kebab-case files, CSS modules over inline styles
+6. **No behaviour changes** — Performance changes must be invisible to users
+
+## What NOT to Do
+
+- Don't make sweeping refactors across many files
+- Don't change visual behaviour or UX
+- Don't add new dependencies without strong justification
+- Don't skip the verification step
+- Don't create a PR if the improvement is negligible or unmeasurable
+
+## Verification
+
+After every fix:
+
+```bash
+npx tsc --noEmit && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build
+```
+
+If verification fails, revert the change and try the next issue instead.
+
+## PR Description
+
+Include in your PR description:
+- **Tier**: Which tier this fix came from
+- **Baseline**: Measurement before the change (build size, bundle diff, etc.)
+- **Fix**: What was changed and why it improves performance
+- **Result**: Measurement after the change
+- **Verification**: Confirmation that all checks pass

commits.message:
Architecture cleanup: worker-only Copilot SDK, orthogonal capabilities, Next 16 (#186)

* docs(phase-0): re-true docs for mandatory worker + Next 16

Phase 0 of the architecture cleanup plan. Aligns docs with the current
state: mandatory Copilot worker, per-user runtime pool, Next.js 16 +
React 19.2.

- README: worker is mandatory, drop 'routes still execute in-process'.
- docs/architecture-multitenant.md: rewrite the Copilot runtime model
  section as current-state-of-the-world; add per-user runtime pool envs;
  add Server Action / Server Component guard rule and cache-key scope
  rule to anti-patterns list.
- .github/copilot-instructions.md: Next.js 14 -> 16 + React 19.2.
- .github/skills/copilot-sdk/SKILL.md: SDK version 1.0.0-beta.4; drop
  stale lib/copilotService.ts reference; require useLoggedInUser: false
  and gitHubToken on every session.
- .github/workflows/daily-*.md: Next.js 14 -> 16 across 4 daily-task
  prompts.
- Add .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md with the tenant-invariant
  checklist (6-item gate from the cleanup plan).
- Mark 5 implemented superpowers plans (worker pool, worker service
  foundation, per-user runtime, mandatory worker, worker job split) as
  Implemented to stop drift.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(phase-1): delete dead in-process Copilot chat path

Web/API chat now exclusively flows through the worker via the execution
boundary; the in-process adapter and its direct session factories were
unreachable in production. Remove:

- src/lib/copilot/execution/in-process.ts (+ test)
- createLoggedChatSession / createLoggedGitHubChatSession from
  src/lib/copilot/server.ts (and dead chat-only helper + prompt imports)
- Stale chat-session asserts and mocks from the public-surface,
  execution-index, and /api/copilot route tests

Net: -303 LOC. Coach session helpers and getConversationSession remain
(focus/evaluation/authoring still run the SDK in-process server-side).
All 1831 tests green, lint clean.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci(phase-2): boundary skill + file-size & test-boundary guardrails

Add a practical contract for tests in this repo and back it with two
failing-mode CI scripts.

Skill: .github/skills/tests-that-respect-boundaries/SKILL.md
  - Test the unit, not the mock (assert on result.current / return value
    / response body / audit-log entry).
  - Mock only at system seams (fetch, fs, timers, env, third-party SDKs).
  - Hook tests use renderHook + result.current — never
    expect(applicationModuleMock).toHaveBeenCalled*.
  - it.each for >=4 similar cases.
  - One module, one test file.
  - 400-LOC budget per test file (450 prod / 500 test cap in CI).
  - Tenant boundary assertions required on guarded routes / per-user
    storage.
  - No new test without a distinct public-behaviour assertion.
  Cross-linked from testing.instructions.md and tdd/SKILL.md.

CI scripts: scripts/check-file-sizes.mjs + check-test-boundaries.mjs
  - File sizes: 450 LOC prod / 500 LOC test, with one-time
    .size-budget-baseline.json grandfathering today's 8 prod + 11 test
    offenders.
  - Test boundaries: forbids toHaveBeenCalled* in test files outside
    src/test/integration/, src/lib/security/, src/lib/auth/ unless
    grandfathered by .test-boundary-baseline.json (52 files, 311
    matchers today).
  - Both baselines are ratchets — current file may shrink, never grow.
    Phase 8 deletes both files when they are empty.
  - Replaces the old scripts/check-file-size.mjs (hand-rolled per-file
    cap dictionary) with a uniform 450/500 contract.

CI wiring: .github/workflows/ci.yml gains a 'Run guardrails' step that
fails the build on any violation, plus an informational debt:unused
report. npm scripts: check:sizes, check:test-boundaries,
check:guardrails.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(phase-3a): single guard primitive + share worker fetch + cover quiz/plan/author

Three converging cleanups landing as one commit, all on the user-facing
authentication & worker-call seams:

1. Guard core extracted (prereq for P7 Server Actions)
   - src/lib/security/guard.ts gains requireGuardedUserContext(opts)
     which returns { ctx, release }. Server Actions and RSC data
     loaders can call this directly to inherit the same rate-limit +
     concurrent-cap + audit policy as API routes.
   - withUserGuards becomes a thin route adapter: it composes the core
     and manages release() in a finally block. No behaviour change for
     existing callers; guard.test.ts continues to pass unchanged.

2. Quiz, guided-plan, challenge/author migrated to withUserGuards
   - All three were AI-backed routes still calling requireUserContext
     directly: no rate limit, no concurrent cap, no audit event for the
     session start. They now share the same guard primitive as
     focus/copilot/suggestions/evaluate/hint.
   - Adds QUIZ_GUARD, PLAN_GUARD, AUTHOR_GUARD presets in
     route-defaults.ts with RATE_LIMIT_{QUIZ,PLAN,AUTHOR}_* env overrides.
   - Both rewrites re-check knownApiErrorResponse before any static
     fallback so entitlement (402) signals are never masked.
   - api-auth-inventory.test.ts updated to assert the new boundaries.

3. Worker HTTP calls consolidated behind one primitive
   - New src/lib/copilot/execution/worker-fetch.ts exposes workerFetch
     and workerFetchJson: shared config resolution, shared-secret
     authorization, W3C trace header propagation, uniform error
     messages, optional allowNotFound.
   - src/app/api/jobs/worker-client.ts (8 endpoints) collapses from
     210 → ~120 LOC; every method now one call.
   - src/app/api/ai-activity/worker-client.ts goes from 40 → 20 LOC.
   - The chat-execution http-client retains its own abort/timeout
     controller (different concerns) and is intentionally not folded
     in.

Net: +108 / -261 LOC across the diff. All 1831 tests green, lint clean,
file-size & test-boundary guardrails clean.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(api): extract buildProfileContext helper

Consolidates the per-request 'get Octokit, build compact profile,
serialize, log on failure' pattern that was duplicated across 4 AI
routes (quiz, guided-plan, suggestions, focus). The helper returns
both the serialized string (used by all four for prompts) and the
structured CompactDeveloperProfile (focus uses it for calibration
suggestions).

Net: -50 LOC across routes, +52 LOC for the helper, but routes are
now responsibility-focused and the graceful-degradation pattern is
defined once.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(api): introduce withGuardedRoute primitive

Every authenticated AI route was hand-rolling the same try/catch +
guardErrorResponse + knownApiErrorResponse mapping around withUserGuards.
This commit adds withGuardedRoute as the single route-shaped adapter
that:

- calls withUserGuards under the hood (auth + rate-limit + session-cap
  + audit)
- catches guard errors via guardErrorResponse (401/402/429)
- re-throws unknown errors so each route's custom fallback path still
  applies (quiz/plan static fallback, hint handleApiError, evaluate +
  author custom 500 with timing)

withUserGuards stays as the lower-level callable for Server Actions /
RSC loaders in Phase 7 where the NextResponse shape doesn't apply.

knownApiErrorResponse is no longer called from the outer catch — it
was always redundant with guardErrorResponse (both map UnauthorizedError
+ entitlement). Inner-block usage in quiz/plan stays put because that
runs BEFORE the static fallback.

Net: -54 LOC across 8 route files.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(focus): extract handlers; route becomes a 48-line shim

Moves prompt selection, parallel sub-component fan-out, the
calibration-suggestions side-channel, fallback shape, and entitlement
re-throw out of the route file and into src/lib/focus/handlers.ts.

Route /api/focus now does only: parse body, call withGuardedRoute,
delegate to generateFocus. From 310 LOC -> 48 LOC.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(profile): extract handler; route becomes 15-line shim

Profile route had two near-duplicate response builders (cached vs
fresh fetch). Both now flow through buildProfileResponse(), with
getRecentActivity() consolidating the try/catch around event fetch.
The whole flow lives in src/lib/github/profile-handler.ts.

Route /api/profile becomes a re-export. From 271 LOC -> 15 LOC.

Also extends the api-auth-inventory test to follow handler imports:
when a route delegates to @/lib/.../handle*Request, the boundary
marker can live in the handler module. Keeps thin route shims valid
without weakening the inventory invariant.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(api): use authErrorResponse/handleUnauthorizedError consistently

Both jobs/route.ts GET handler and workspace/storage/list/route.ts were
duplicating the 'instanceof UnauthorizedError → 401' boilerplate inline.
Route them through the existing shared primitives from src/lib/api/auth-errors.

- jobs/route.ts: use authErrorResponse() to short-circuit before the
  worker-failure 503 fallback.
- workspace/storage/list/route.ts: use handleUnauthorizedError() which
  returns the 401 response or rethrows.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs: document withGuardedRoute + layered guard primitives

The guard module now exposes three layered primitives (core, transport-
agnostic wrapper, route adapter). Update the multi-tenant architecture
doc and copilot-instructions to reflect the new public surface so
contributors know which one to reach for from API routes vs. Server
Actions vs. RSC data loaders.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(activity): use workerFetchJson primitive in logger-client

Removes duplicated config/auth/header wiring (requireConfig, buildHeaders,
raw fetch calls) and routes both postEvent + patchEvent through the
shared workerFetchJson primitive. The swallow-errors behaviour stays —
activity logging must never block AI work — but the transport layer
is now centralized.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(next16): rename middleware.ts -> proxy.ts + add maxDuration to SSE routes

Next 16 deprecated middleware.ts in favor of proxy.ts. Rename file +
test + symbol (middleware -> proxy / authMiddleware -> authProxy) and
fix the docstrings/comments that referenced the old name.

Add export const maxDuration = 300 to every long-running route:
- /api/copilot (AI chat)
- /api/challenge/author + /api/challenge/evaluate (SSE)
- /api/ai-activity/stream + /api/internal/ai-activity/stream (SSE)
- /api/jobs/[id]/stream + /api/internal/jobs/[id]/stream (SSE)

Default 10s timeout would cut streaming clients off mid-token.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(storage): use authErrorResponse in storage factory + workspace route

Replace the inline 'instanceof UnauthorizedError → 401 JSON' boilerplate
in createStorageRoute and workspace/storage with the shared
authErrorResponse() primitive, removing duplicated NextResponse.json
construction. Consistent treatment now across every per-user route.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(hooks): extract useOperationRegenerations from use-ai-focus

Pull the three useSyncExternalStore subscriptions to the global
operationsManager (topic/challenge/goal regenerations) into a
dedicated hook. The seam between focus-fetch lifecycle and
cross-component visibility is now testable in isolation.

use-ai-focus drops from 558 -> 541 LOC; baseline tightened.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(hooks): split use-challenge-sandbox into focused sub-hooks

Extracted three single-responsibility hooks from use-challenge-sandbox
(628 LOC) per rubber-duck-reviewed Phase 6 plan:

- use-evaluation: polling, mount recovery, job cancellation. Uses a
  generation token so resetEvaluation() ignores late polling responses
  (latent race in the prior implementation). Takes a lazy getFiles()
  accessor so the evaluate() callback identity stays stable across
  keystrokes.
- use-hints: progressive hint conversation. Takes getCurrentCode() so
  fast file switches between user actions resolve correctly.
- use-solution-generation: debug-mode AI solver.

use-challenge-sandbox becomes a thin coordinator (102 LOC) that
composes useWorkspace + the three sub-hooks and orchestrates reset.
Public return shape is preserved; consumers (ChallengeSandbox.tsx,
hint-display, ResultsPanel, evaluation-result-display) unchanged.

Baseline tightened: use-challenge-sandbox removed from baseline.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(hooks): extract chat-stream sub-hooks into focused files

Per rubber-duck-reviewed Phase 6 plan, promote the three already-isolated
inline functions in use-learning-chat-stream.ts (616 LOC) into named
files. No behaviour change — the file already contained the right
seams; this exposes them as importable modules.

- chat-stream-events.ts: SSEStreamEvent type, buildTerminalHandler,
  dispatchFrame. Pure dispatch helpers, no React.
- use-chat-sse-subscriptions.ts: opens one SSE per active chat job,
  surfaces reconnecting state. Chat-specific (rubber-duck flagged that
  consumeSSE is already the generic primitive, so no useSSESubscription).
- use-pending-stream-reconciler.ts: pendingStreamMessages reconciler.
- use-orphaned-chat-stream-finalizer.ts: STALE_STREAM_THRESHOLD safety
  net, renamed from useStaleStreamFinalizer per rubber-duck (the
  prior name implied heartbeat detection; behaviour is orphan-thread
  cleanup, not stale-stream reconnect).

use-learning-chat-stream.ts is now a 284-LOC coordinator that owns
the cross-cutting derivations (streamingThreadIdsKey,
chatSubscriptionKey, isStreaming) and the public action surface. All
38 chat-stream tests pass unchanged.

Baseline: use-learning-chat-stream removed from production budget.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat(hooks): useStoreQuery primitive + migrate useSpacedRepCandidates

Per Specialist-Test-reviewed Phase 5 plan, introduce a single hook for
the duplicated useState+useEffect+try/catch+isActive-flag pattern that
appears in useThreads, useCustomChallengeQueue, useSpacedRepCandidates,
useUserProfile, and useGuidedPlan.

useStoreQuery<T>:
- data/isLoading/error/refresh return shape
- ref-based query/onLoaded so changing function identity does not
  re-fire the load
- aborted-signal pattern replaces the per-hook isActive flag
- onLoaded errors are isolated (data + caller state stay valid)
- deps array drives re-runs explicitly

11 behavioural tests in use-store-query.test.ts (canonical exemplar
for the tests-that-respect-boundaries skill: no mocks of the module
under test, all assertions on result.current).

Migrated useSpacedRepCandidates as the smallest consumer: 51 -> 38 LOC.
Remaining migrations (useThreads, useCustomChallengeQueue, useUserProfile,
useGuidedPlan) will land as the corresponding tests are rewritten in
the same Phase 5 wave.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(focus): extract storage helpers, slim coordinator class

Split src/lib/focus/storage.ts (633 LOC) into:
- storage.ts (209 LOC) - thin read-mutate-write coordinator
- storage-transitions.ts (263 LOC) - state machine transitions
- storage-mutations.ts (119 LOC) - add/remove/read helpers

Public API of focusStore singleton preserved; all 99 focus tests
plus 1842/1842 full suite pass. Removes storage.ts from size budget
baseline (5 production files remaining).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(copilot,jobs): extract streaming + jobs storage internals

- src/lib/copilot/streaming.ts: 625→142 LOC.
  Public factories now delegate to streaming-session.ts (createGenericStreamingSession)
  which itself uses streaming-telemetry.ts (StreamContext, pumpEventQueue, terminal recorders).

- src/lib/jobs/storage.ts: 579→334 LOC.
  Types, schema validation, load/save, mutex, cleanup, and mutateJob moved to
  storage-internals.ts so the public jobStorage object stays under the size budget.

Both removed from size-budget baseline (3 production files remaining).
All 1842 tests pass; lint clean.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(focus,skills): slim use-ai-focus + skills/page

- src/hooks/use-ai-focus.ts: 541→319 LOC. Skip/regen flows extracted to
  use-focus-skip.ts (194); storage refresh effects to
  use-focus-storage-subscriptions.ts (69).

- src/app/skills/page.tsx: 503→195 LOC. State + mutators extracted to
  use-skills-profile.ts (191); sidebar + skills list extracted to
  _components/{SkillsSidebar,SkillsList}.tsx.

Both removed from size-budget baseline (1 production file remaining:
active-operations.ts at 725).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* refactor(operations): split active-operations manager into focused modules

active-operations.ts: 725 → 446 LOC. The manager class is now a thin
orchestrator that wires together purpose-built helper modules.

Extractions:
- job-poller.ts (92): pollJobUntilTerminal() owns the GET /api/jobs/[id]
  loop and surfaces terminal transitions as PollJobCallbacks events.
  Knows nothing about operations, snapshots, or React.
- restore-active-jobs.ts (69): fetchActiveJobEntries() owns the
  browser/SSR fork for replaying pending jobs at init time.
- chat-job-registry.ts (119): registerExistingChatJob /
  completeExistingChatJob own the SSE-tracked chat-job lifecycle.
  Manager hands over a narrow ChatJobRegistryState interface.
- operation-poll-callbacks.ts (84): buildJobPollCallbacks() owns the
  terminal-decision-to-state-transition translation (durable handler
  first, user onComplete second, delayed cleanup last).
- job-types.ts (11): shared JobResponse shape.

Removes active-operations.ts from .size-budget-baseline.json — the
production baseline is now empty. Phase 6 size-budget burndown complete.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci(guardrails): land Phase 7 cache + fetch + server-action scripts

Three new CI scripts that police the tenancy contract for the upcoming
cacheComponents and reactCompiler flips:

- scripts/check-cache-key-scope.mjs — every cacheTag/revalidateTag/
  updateTag literal must be tenant-scoped (interpolated userId/
  sessionId/installationId/owner) or prefixed 'public:'.
- scripts/check-server-fetch-tenancy.mjs — every server-side fetch()
  must declare cache: 'no-store' | next.tags | force-cache, use a non-
  GET method, or carry a // public-cache: <reason> justification.
- scripts/check-server-action-guards.mjs — every exported async in a
  'use server' file must call requireGuardedUserContext() or carry a
  // public-action: <reason> justification. Name-based allowlists are
  explicitly not acceptable.

Fixed pre-existing violations these scripts surfaced:
- 6 server-side GET fetch() sites annotated with cache: 'no-store'
  (worker proxies, SSE producers, api-client, restore-active-jobs).
- 2 auth Server Actions (signOutAction, signInWithGitHub) annotated
  with // public-action: justifications.
- use-store-query.test.ts baselined (assertions are on user-supplied
  callbacks that form the hook's API contract, not on service mocks).

Wired into package.json (check:guardrails) and .github/workflows/ci.yml.
All 5 guardrails pass on the current codebase.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(use-custom-challenge-queue): rewrite as behavior-based, 807 → 297 LOC

Replace store-mock-call assertions with renderHook + result.current
assertions. Mock only at the api-client seam; let the real
